title: Almine Rech New York presents James Turrell's first U.S. exhibition with the gallery
summary: Almine Rech New York is presenting James Turrell's first exhibition with the gallery in the United States. On view from November 12, 2026 to January 30, 2027, it marks the artist's thirteenth exhibition with Almine Rech in more than three decades of collaboration. Featuring over fifteen works, this presentation includes a new Shallow Space, as well as new pieces from the Glassworks series and a new Cross Corner work. These additions to landmark bodies of work continue Turrell's relentless exploration of space and light, encouraging viewers to pay close attention to their own senses. In 1989, Almine Rech organized Turrell's first gallery exhibition in Europe, presenting a Light Piece entitled Blood Lust at her gallery in Paris. Today, after over thirty years of collaboration, this exhibition attests to the enduring relationship between the artist and the gallery, as well as Turrell's ongoing dedication to his abiding creative watch

title: Christie's New York Marquee Week Live sales total $967.2 million
summary: Christie's 20/21 Fall Marquee Week in New York concluded its live sales on Friday, November 20 at Rockefeller Center with a strong Post-War and Contemporary Art Day Sale, which totaled $115,058,640—the second highest total ever in the sale's history—selling 87% by lot and 89% by value. The three-session sale began with a dedicated session of works from the collection of Herbert Lust, which sold for $8.7 million, and was led by Figure in Landscape I by Willem de Kooning, which sold for $4.4 million. The successful Post-War and Contemporary Day Sale followed Thursday night's 21st Century Evening Sale in the category, which achieved $146 million, and a marathon of auctions on Wednesday, which saw the highest total in Christie's history for the Impressionist and Modern Art Day and Works on Paper, with $79.7 million across both sales. title: Online exhibition pairs Wayne Sorce's early Chicago night scenes with large-format color cityscapes
summary: Joseph Bellows Gallery announces Wayne Sorce: Black & White & Color, an online exhibition bringing together the artist's early black-and-white photographs of Chicago and his later large-format color photographs of Chicago and New York. Wayne Sorce (American, 1946–2015) developed a distinctive body of work examining the American urban landscape. His photographs are distinguished by their rigorous compositions, attention to architectural form, and complex organization of pictorial space. Working in both black-and-white and color, Sorce approached the city as a subject for sustained photographic investigation, revealing the visual relationships between buildings, streets, light, and the surrounding environment. Sorce's early black-and-white photographs, made in Chicago during the late 1960s and early 1970s, frequently depict the city at night. title: Qatar Museums unveils Gerhard Richter's Doha Pavilion
summary: Qatar Museums (QM) today unveiled Doha Pavilion: Gerhard Richter, a new permanent, site-specific structure conceived and designed by the world-renowned artist as a freestanding work of art and architecture. Sited in Doha’s MIA Park, the expansive public space outside the Museum of Islamic Art, Doha Pavilion was realised in collaboration with Selldorf Architects and houses a distinct body of Richter's paintings and sculptures including a new work created for the Pavilion. A legacy initiative of the Qatar-Germany 2017 Year of Culture, Doha Pavilion joins a host of major public artworks in MIA Park by world-renowned artists, such as Richard Serra, Nairy Baghramian, and Peter Fischli and David Weiss, among others. title: The James Museum debuts uncommon side-by-side photographic prints by Edward Curtis
summary: The James Museum of Western & Wildlife Art has rotated a rare selection of original Edward Curtis photographs into its permanent collection galleries for a focused installation titled The Art of the Print with Edward Curtis, on view now through late April. Drawn from the museum’s Curtis holdings—among the largest in the nation—the installation presents an exceptionally uncommon look at how a single negative transforms across multiple printing processes. While antique photography collections are housed in institutions nationwide, this is a rare opportunity to view different historical printing methods struck from the exact same negative side by side. Few photographers master more than one or two photographic processes. Edward Curtis worked skillfully in five: platinum printing, photogravure, gold-toned printing-out-paper, orotone, and gelatin silver printing. title: National Gallery of Canada receives exceptional gift of modern and contemporary glass works
summary: The National Gallery of Canada announced today a landmark promised gift from Charles and the late Andrea Bronfman. Comprising 56 works of modern and contemporary glass together with an endowment fund, the donation will significantly transform the NGC holdings and set the stage for a new chapter in decorative arts and design. The grouping features artists from Canada, Europe, the United States and Asia, including seven Canadian artists and seven women. A selection of the glass works is now on view at the Gallery through April 30, 2027. The endowment will enable the creation of a curatorial position dedicated to decorative arts and design at the NGC. “For more than a century, members of the Bronfman family have championed cultural initiatives in Canada and around the world. title: William Turner Gallery presents new gold-leaf paintings by Mark Steven Greenfield
summary: William Turner Gallery is presenting We Will Not Be Erased, an exhibition of new paintings by Mark Steven Greenfield and his third solo presentation with the gallery. Continuing his acclaimed Halo series, Greenfield brings extraordinary Black lives out of history’s margins and into the luminous foreground. At a moment when the telling of Black history is itself under attack, these paintings assert an unequivocal refusal: these lives mattered. Their stories will not be erased. The exhibition advances an artistic inquiry that has acquired increasing urgency across three successive exhibitions. In the fall of 2020, following the murder of George Floyd and the nationwide Black Lives Matter protests, Greenfield’s Black Madonna exhibition made a sensational debut at the gallery. title: Wardha Shabbir explores hybrid life forms and sensory spaces at Sabrina Amrani Projects
summary: Sabrina Amrani is presenting The Kind We Become, the second solo show by Wardha Shabbir in the gallery at Sabrina Amrani Projects. During her childhood in Lahore, Wardha Shabbir (Lahore, Pakistan, 1987) used to hide in the garden. She spent so much time in that secluded space that it eventually became a kind of provisional home from which, away from the gaze of others, she observed the tiny leaves, followed the movements of ants and paused to notice the irregularities of plants. Over time, this attention to the small and to what escapes a first glance gradually took shape as a working method and a discipline that underpin her entire artistic practice, from painting to sculpture, installation, animation and exhibition environments. In her works, repetition and accumulation incorporate time into the production process and demand sustained attention from the viewer, a way of looking that is not exhausted by the first encounter. title: Patricia Perez Eustaquio examines trade, colonial history, and material labor in new exhibition at Silverlens
summary: Working across unexpected mediums and disciplines, Patricia Perez Eustaquio has long examined materials with histories linked to memory and physical labor. The title is taken from a practice in the Philippines' prehistoric economy, when Sulu natural pearls were bartered for metalware and weapons. The literal phrase is an apt metaphor for trade and colonial history: what gets exchanged, who decides what is valuable, and what indigenous knowledge gets forgotten in the process. The title also operates as a sharp play on the common idiom, "pearls before swine." Where the traditional saying warns against wasting valuable things on those incapable of appreciating them, maybe Eustaquio's version asks us to think about another proposition: the act of surrendering something rare and organic, such as natural pearls, in exchange for an instrument of coercion. title: Esther Schipper Seoul presents Ryan Gander's gallery debut in South Korea
summary: Esther Schipper, Seoul presents Joy / The structure of feeling / Be with me always, take any form, Ryan Gander's first exhibition in our Seoul gallery and the fourth with the gallery. Ryan Gander's practice transgresses general definitions of medium or approach. At the core of Gander's work is the question of what form an idea can take to become a work of art. Playfully post-conceptual, Gander presents works that employ the appearance of everyday objects or draw on common experiences to create situations in which the meaning of the objects on view is changed—and with it the experience of the observer. This was the case in early September with The Find, when Gander had 16,000 small coins dispersed throughout Seoul's city streets. The nickel coins became treasured objects. title: Pace Gallery announces booth highlights for Art Basel Miami Beach 2026
summary: At the 2026 edition of Art Basel Miami Beach, Pace will present key historical works by Alexander Calder, David Hockney, Louise Nevelson, Kenneth Noland, Richard Pousette-Dart, and Lucas Samaras together with new and recent works by Lynda Benglis, Elmgreen & Dragset, Torkwase Dyson, Loie Hollowell, Friedrich Kunath, Alicja Kwade, Asher Liftin, Robert Longo, Robert Nava, Lauren Quin, Julian Schnabel, Arlene Shechet, Mika Tajima, James Turrell, Hank Willis Thomas, and Anicka Yi, among others. title: British painter Louise Giovanelli explores cinematic illusion and theatrical light in new London show
summary: ‘In the Light of False Suns’, Louise Giovanelli’s exhibition of new paintings at White Cube Mason’s Yard, revisits subjects long central to the artist’s practice, casting them here beneath a borrowed light. The exhibition takes its title from parhelia, or ‘false suns’, an atmospheric optical phenomenon in which sunlight refracted through ice crystals produces bright spots on either side of the sun. Illusory and dependent on the true sun, they are ‘companions of light rather than its origin’, as Giovanelli puts it.1 In these works, the false sun becomes a figure for the seductive, artificial illumination of cinema, theatrical spectacle and religious iconography, as well as the shifting play of light upon the painted surface. title: Curators Jean de Loisy and Margaux Bonopera examine artistic reinvention and archives in 'HARVESTS'
summary: The exhibition HARVESTS is inspired by Vincent van Gogh's collection of images and books, which includes more than five thousand items and is now held in the collection of the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam. Comprised of rare editions and cheap copies, etchings and banal images clipped from newspapers, and paintings and prints acquired with his brother, as well as books on art, poetry, and literature in several languages, it constitutes a kind of "Imaginary Museum" whose riches he would constantly mine, and that he would comment on at length in his letters. Van Gogh's taste for artistic images was developed even before he made the decision to become an artist, during the four years in which he worked in the very large outposts of Goupil & Cie. in The Hague, London, and Paris. title: Esker Foundation publishes Jana Sterbak: Dimensions of Intimacy
summary: Among Canada’s most renowned and influential artists, Jana Sterbak’s 47-year career has spanned sculpture, video, installation and performance. This publication is an opportunity to further explore Sterbak’s pivotal contributions to art through the reflections of 16 curators and art historians: Chloé Ariot, Sandra Barré, Catherine Bédard, Mojeanne Behzadi, Ray Cronin, Elizabeth Diggon, Mireille Eagan, Ihor Holubizky, Magdalena Holzhey, Melanie O’Brian, Naomi Potter, Diana Sherlock, Johanne Sloan, Anne-Marie St-Jean Aubre, Shauna Thompson, and Adam Welch. title: Huge gilded statue of Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius once stood in southern Scotland
summary: New research has revealed that a massive monument to the Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius once stood in the Scottish Borders. The grand sculpture is the only known example from Scotland and the findings rewrite our understanding of the northern-most frontier of the Roman Empire. The statue has been reconstructed using its surviving gilded bronze leg ahead of a major new exhibition opening at the National Museum of Scotland this weekend; Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire. Discovered in a bog in Milsington near Hawick in 1820, the larger than life-sized lower leg with a boot-clad foot dates to the AD 140s and is one of the most striking treasures from Roman Britain in National Museums Scotland's collection. For over two centuries it was assumed to be loot from further south, perhaps the major Roman town of York, Eboracum.

title: Group exhibition 'HNTRLND' examines the rural periphery as a social, political, and cultural construct
summary: The group exhibition HNTRLND explores the “hinterland” as a multilayered social, political, and cultural construct. The starting point is the observation that rural and peripheral areas are often imagined as the opposite of urban centers. They are considered places of stability and manageability and are seen as authentic. However, they are simultaneously regarded as areas of structural disadvantage, social disengagement, and political radicalization. This exhibition critically examines these attributions while exploring the actual conditions and ideological transformations of such spaces. In this context, “hinterland” is understood not solely in geographical terms but also as a metaphorical space. title: David Zwirner presents Ethiopian-born Italian painter Jem Perucchini's U.S. debut in Tribeca
summary: David Zwirner is presenting an exhibition of new paintings and works on paper by Italian, Ethiopian-born painter Jem Perucchini at the gallery’s Tribeca location in New York. Following recent solo presentations at Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, Turin, and Centro Andaluz de Arte Contemporáneo, Seville, this is the artist’s first exhibition in the United States. The exhibition takes its title from a painting on view, Sospiro (2026), which translates from Italian as “sigh.” A sigh—at once a breath, a pause, a release, a gesture—holds significance for Perucchini because of its qualities both essential and transient, audible and invisible. As the artist describes, this fleeting moment of vitality represents “the passage between the inner self and the external world, between soul and body, between what is held within and what is released.”¹

title: Bangkok artist Tanat Teeradakorn debuts first institutional solo exhibition in China at Shanghai's CHERUBY
summary: Memory Threshold: Chaos Resonance presents Bangkok-based artist Tanat Teeradakorn’s first institutional solo exhibition in China, following a two-month residency at CHERUBY in Shanghai. Transforming CHERUBY’s 1939 building into an immersive, multi-layered installation, the exhibition takes its title from the commissioned film. Trained in design and shaped by music production, Teeradakorn works across moving image, sound, performance and installation. His practice examines historical memory and the political tensions that emerge when binary oppositions harden into paralysis, approaching the body, sound and merchandise as mediums through which cultural meanings are produced and transformed. title: Museum Folkwang announces exhibition program 2027
summary: Since its founding, Museum Folkwang has continually evolved through new artistic perspectives, unexpected connections and a commitment to exploring the cultural questions of its time. The 2027 exhibition programme brings together diverse artistic positions, historical perspectives and approaches to seeing, reflecting the museum’s ongoing dialogue between art, society and the world around us. One of the programme’s highlights is Wangechi Mutu: To soothe your Golden gilt, a major exhibition dedicated to one of the most influential artists of our time. Her artistic practice encompasses sculpture, collage, painting, drawing, video, performance and installation. The exhibition focuses on her sculptural oeuvre, which has rarely been presented on a comparable scale in Europe. It traces the development of Mutu’s tremendously experimental and diverse

title: Miguel Fernández de Castro joins Travesía Cuatro
summary: Travesía Cuatro announced that they are now representing Miguel Fernández de Castro. Miguel Fernández de Castro’s (Sonora, Mexico. 1986) artistic practice stems from research deeply rooted in the territory he inhabits, the Sonora-Arizona border region. Drawing on its landscapes and material remains, Fernández de Castro explores the traces left by different forms of occupation, control and transformation of the territory, paying attention to the traces, the absences and that which remains outside the usual frameworks of representation. Through photography, video, sculpture and writing, he investigates the forms in which ecological and violent regimes intertwine in the production of space and memory. Since 2018, he has worked with groups searching for missing people to document clandestine graves on both sides of the Mexico–US border.

title: Extensive art of Mary Blair collection leads Heritage's 'Great Artists of the Walt Disney Studio' auction
summary: More than 70 works by Disney Legend Mary Blair, including a major selection from the Richard Kraft Collection, lead Heritage Auctions’ The Art of Disney Signature® Auction, Dec. 11–14. Spanning Blair’s career with Disney, the collection includes concept art for celebrated films and Disneyland’s “it’s a small world” attraction. Blair’s distinctive use of color and shape helped define the visual identity of films including Dumbo, The Adventures of Ichabod and Mr. Toad, Cinderella, Alice in Wonderland and Peter Pan. The auction also features Blair art connected to Melody Time, The Three Caballeros and Song of the South. Two thirds of the Blair works come from Kraft’s collection, widely regarded as one of the largest private collections of her art. title: Galerie Nathalie Obadia presents French artist Victoria Palacios' first solo exhibition in Paris
summary: Galerie Nathalie Obadia is presenting Victoria Palacios’ first solo exhibition in Paris. The French artist lives and works in Brussels, where she studied painting and performance. Also active internationally as a musician and performer, she has developed a practice in which painting becomes a space for theatrical staging. Following Des signes, des scènes, her exhibition at the gallery in Brussels in 2024, she unveils a new body of nearly fifty works in which figures, costumes, materials and props proliferate, like remnants of a theatre still inhabited by its performers. Within this meticulously orchestrated universe, perspectives multiply: from backstage, onstage or in the audience, each vantage point gives rise to a different narrative. title: Elite serial number 1 banknotes head to Heritage's World Paper Money Auction
summary: The very first example of an exceptionally rare type, from one of the world’s elite collections of banknotes, will be among the top attractions in Heritage’s Dec. 5–6 World Paper Money Signature® Auction–Hong Kong. Two Serial Number 1 rarities from The Peh Family Collection Part VI offer extraordinary links to a banknote series whose introduction was derailed by World War II: the Malaya Board of Commissioners of Currency 5 Dollars 1.1.1940, PMG About Uncirculated 55 EPQ and 1 Dollar 1.1.1940, PMG Choice About Unc 58 EPQ. Intended to replace Straits Settlements currency, the inaugural Malaya series comprised $1, $5 and $10 denominations dated Jan. 1, 1940, but only the $10 entered normal circulation. Shipments of the lower denominations were lost at sea or captured by Japanese forces, while remaining supplies were held in India
